messages.content: Why does a spoon left in a hot pan of dal get too hot to touch?
Because metal carries heat well, the spoon gets hot. Heat travels along the metal from the hot dal up to the handle, so the part in your hand warms up too.
Why do clothes dry faster on a windy day?
Wind speeds up drying. Because moving air carries away the water vapour that rises from the cloth, so more water can keep leaving instead of the air around the cloth becoming damp.
Why does ice float in a glass of water?
Ice floats because it is lighter than the same amount of water. Water spreads out a little as it freezes, so ice takes up more room for its weight and stays on top.
Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
Light reaches us first. Because light travels far faster than sound, so the flash arrives almost at once while the rumble is still on its way.
Why does a plant on a windowsill bend towards the window?
It is reaching for light. Because plants need light to make food, and the stem grows faster on the shaded side, which tips the top towards the brighter side.
Why do puddles disappear after the rain stops and the sun comes out?
The water dries up into the air. Because the sun's warmth turns the water into invisible vapour, which rises and mixes with the air.
Why does a metal bench feel colder than a wooden bench on a winter morning?
The metal feels colder to your hand. Because metal pulls heat out of your skin faster than wood does, even though both benches are the same temperature.
Why does a heavy iron ship float but a small iron nail sinks?

The ship floats because of its shape. Because it is hollow and pushes aside a huge amount of water, and that water pushes back up hard enough to hold the ship, while the nail pushes aside very little.
Why does your voice echo in an empty hall?
Sound bounces back to you. Because the hard walls and bare floor reflect sound waves instead of soaking them up, so you hear your voice again a moment later.
Why do we see our face in still water but not in a muddy puddle that is being stirred?
Still water acts like a mirror. Because a smooth surface sends light back in an orderly way, while a stirred surface scatters it in many directions.
Why does a balloon rubbed on your hair stick to the wall?
Rubbing gives the balloon an electric charge. Because the charged balloon pulls on the tiny charges in the wall, and that small pull is enough to hold such a light thing in place.
Why do we feel cooler when we stand in front of a fan on a hot day?
The moving air helps your sweat dry. Because sweat takes heat from your skin as it dries, and the fan makes it dry faster. The fan does not cool the air itself.
Why does bread go hard if it is left out uncovered?
It loses its moisture. Because the water in the bread slowly escapes into the air, and without it the crumb turns dry and stiff.
Why do shadows get longer in the evening?
The sun is low in the sky. Because light then comes in at a slant, so objects block it over a longer stretch of ground.
A rainbow needs both sun and rain. Why?
Sunlight needs raindrops to split it. Because each drop bends and bounces the light inside, and that separates it into its colours. Without drops or without sun, there is nothing to split.
Why does a kettle whistle when the water boils?
Steam is forced out through a small opening. Because the rushing steam makes the air at the spout vibrate, and vibrating air is what we hear as a whistle.
Why does milk spoil faster in a warm kitchen than in the fridge?
Warmth speeds up spoiling. Because the germs in milk multiply faster when it is warm, and the cold slows them down.
Why do the leaves of many trees fall in autumn?
The tree is getting ready for the cold season. Because it stops feeding the leaves, which then dry up and drop, so the tree loses less water when the ground is dry or frozen.
Why does a rubber ball bounce but a lump of clay does not?
Rubber springs back into shape. Because it squashes when it hits the floor and then pushes itself out again, while clay stays squashed and keeps the energy as a dent.
Why is it dangerous to touch an electric switch with wet hands?
It can give you a shock. Because water carries electricity well, so wet skin lets current pass through your body more easily.
Why do we wear dark clothes less often in hot, sunny weather?
Dark cloth gets warmer. Because dark colours soak up more of the sun's light and turn it into heat, while light colours send more of it back.
Why does a pot lid rattle when the water inside boils hard?
Steam pushes up on the lid. Because the steam needs somewhere to go, so it lifts the lid a little, and the lid drops back again and again.
Why do roots grow downwards and shoots grow upwards?
Each part is guided by what it needs. Because roots look for water and hold the plant steady, while shoots grow towards light, and a plant senses gravity and light to tell which way to go.
Why does a candle go out when you put a glass over it?
It runs out of fresh air. Because fire needs oxygen to burn, and the small amount trapped under the glass is soon used up.
Why does salt water feel different from fresh water when you swim?
You float more easily in salty water. Because salt makes the water heavier for the same amount, so it pushes up on you harder.
Why do we get goosebumps when we are cold?
Tiny muscles pull the hairs upright. Because the body is trying to trap a layer of warm air against the skin, and that reaction is left over from when our ancestors had thicker hair.
A mirror makes writing look back to front. What is the reason?
The mirror sends light straight back to you. Because the reflection of a page turned towards the mirror faces you the way you would see it if you stood behind the page, so the letters look reversed.
Why do wet roads look shiny at night?
Water fills the tiny bumps in the road. Because a smooth wet surface reflects car headlights like a mirror instead of scattering them.
Why does steam come out of a hot cup of tea?
Tiny drops of water are forming above the cup. Because the invisible vapour from the tea meets cooler air and turns back into small droplets we can see.
Why do some plants need to be watered less often than others?
It depends on how they store water. Because plants like cactus keep water in thick stems and have waxy skin that stops it escaping, while thin-leaved plants lose water quickly.
Why do cold drinks make the outside of a bottle drip?
The air touching the bottle gets chilled. Because cool air cannot hold as much water vapour, so the extra turns into drops on the cold surface.
Why does a magnet pick up a pin but not a pencil?
The pin is made of iron or steel. Because magnets pull on a few metals such as iron, while wood and graphite do not respond to them.
Why does it feel hotter in a closed car parked in the sun?
Heat gets trapped inside. Because sunlight passes through the glass and warms the seats, and the warmth cannot easily get out through the closed windows.
Why do fish need water to breathe, and we do not?
Fish take in air that is dissolved in water. Because their gills are built to pick out that oxygen, while our lungs are built for oxygen in the open air.
Why do we blow on hot soup to cool it?
Blowing makes the soup cool quicker. Because the breath pushes away the warm steam above the soup and helps the heat leave the surface.
Why does honey pour slowly while water pours fast?
Honey is much thicker. Because its tiny parts cling to each other and resist moving past one another, so it flows more slowly.
Why does a dropped feather fall slower than a stone?
Air slows the feather more. Because the feather is light and wide, so the air pushes against it strongly compared with its weight, while the stone cuts through easily.
Why do dogs pant on a hot day?
Panting helps them cool down. Because dogs have few sweat glands, so water evaporating from the tongue and mouth carries heat away.
Why do we hear the sea in a seashell?
The sound comes from the room, not the sea. Because the hollow shell makes the faint noises around you louder at certain pitches, and that blend sounds like waves.
Why do the bottoms of cooking pots often turn black over a gas flame?
Soot sticks to them. Because the flame does not burn all the fuel perfectly, and tiny bits of unburnt carbon settle on the cool pot.
Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?
The sharp knife puts all the push on a very thin edge. Because a small area under the same force presses much harder, so it parts the food easily.
Why does the moon seem to change shape through the month?
We see different amounts of its sunlit side. Because the moon circles the earth, and from our view more or less of the lit half faces us as it moves.
Why do we need to shake a bottle of mango juice that has settled?
The thick parts sink to the bottom. Because they are heavier than the watery part, so they slowly drift down when the bottle stands still.
Why do rooms feel warmer when many people are inside?
Each person gives off heat. Because our bodies make warmth all the time, and in a closed room it adds up with nowhere to go.
Why does a squeaky door get quiet after a drop of oil?
The oil lets the parts slide smoothly. Because the squeak comes from metal rubbing on metal, and oil makes a slippery film between them.
Why does a spinning top stay up while it spins but fall when it stops?
Its spinning keeps it upright. Because a fast spinning object resists being tipped over, and once friction slows it, that resistance fades and gravity wins.
Why do we see stars at night but not in the daytime?
They are still there in the day. Because sunlight scatters in the air and makes the sky so bright that the faint stars cannot be seen against it.
Why does ghee become solid in cold weather?
It is a fat that sets when cooled. Because the fat parts pack closer together as they lose warmth, so the liquid stiffens, and it melts again when it warms.
Why does a stick look bent when it is half in water?
The light bends as it leaves the water. Because light changes direction when it moves between water and air, so the part under water appears in a different place.
Why do trees along a river often grow taller and greener?
They have steady water. Because roots near a river can always drink, so the trees can keep growing even when the land away from it is dry.
Why do we put a lid on a pot when we want water to boil sooner?
The lid keeps the heat in. Because it stops warm steam from escaping, so the water gains heat faster than it loses it.
Why is the sky blue on a clear day?
Air scatters blue light more than the other colours. Because sunlight has all colours mixed, and the blue part gets bounced around the sky in every direction, so it reaches our eyes from everywhere.
My friend went quiet after I laughed at her answer in class. What might she be feeling?
She is probably hurt or embarrassed. Because she may have thought you were laughing at her, and being laughed at in front of others stings even when no harm was meant.
Is it polite to say thank you to a bus conductor?
Yes, it is. Because he is doing a job that helps you, and a thank you shows you noticed his effort, which makes the day pleasant for both of you.
Why do people go quiet when someone starts crying?
They are unsure what to say. Because they do not want to make things worse, and many people feel that staying close and silent is kinder than saying the wrong thing.
What should I do if I accidentally break a classmate's pencil box?
Tell your classmate right away and say sorry. Because hiding it makes the trust weaker once it comes out, while an honest apology lets you offer to put things right.
Why do we knock before entering someone's room?
Knocking gives the person a chance to be ready. Because everyone needs some privacy, and walking in suddenly can embarrass them or interrupt something important.
A boy kept interrupting the teacher. Why might the others get annoyed?
They are losing time and attention. Because when one person keeps talking over the teacher, the whole class cannot hear the lesson, and it feels unfair to those waiting their turn.
Why do people feel nervous before a new school year starts?
The new year brings things they cannot predict. Because they wonder about new teachers, new classmates and harder work, and the mind tends to worry about what it does not know yet.
Why is it kind to share your tiffin with a friend who forgot hers?
It lets her eat when she would otherwise go hungry. Because hunger makes it hard to enjoy the day or to learn, and helping her shows that you care, so she is likely to help you someday.
What does it usually mean when someone avoids looking you in the eye after an argument?
They may feel awkward or ashamed. Because after a fight people are often unsure how to face the other person, and looking away is a way to avoid that discomfort. It does not always mean anger.
Why should you wait for everyone to be served before you start eating at a family meal?
It shows respect for the others. Because starting alone can seem greedy and leaves people feeling left out, while waiting makes the meal a shared event.
If two friends want the same swing, what is a fair way to settle it?
Take turns. Because a turn lets each person enjoy the swing, and when both agree to the rule beforehand, nobody feels cheated.
Why do we feel better after telling a trusted person about a problem?
Sharing makes the problem feel lighter. Because we no longer hold it alone, and the listener may offer comfort or a new way to look at it.
Why do people clap at the end of a performance?
Clapping is a way to say well done. Because the performers worked hard and want to know the audience enjoyed it, and a shared sound lets everyone show thanks together.
Is it wise to say yes to everything a new friend asks?
No, it is better to think first. Because some requests may not suit you or may be unfair, and a good friend will accept a polite no without getting upset.
My cousin never says sorry, even when she is wrong. Why might she find it hard?
Saying sorry may feel like losing. Because some people link admitting a mistake with being weak or shamed, so they avoid it, and they may need gentle practice to feel safe doing it.
In a library, why do people talk softly?
Quiet lets people concentrate. Because loud talk carries across a room and breaks the focus of readers, and a library exists so that everyone can read in peace.
Why might a child feel jealous when a new baby arrives at home?
The child fears getting less attention. Because everyone is suddenly busy with the baby, and the child does not yet understand that love is not used up when it is shared.
A friend borrowed my notebook and returned it with a torn page. How should I bring it up?
Tell her calmly what happened and how you feel. Because blaming her will make her defensive, while a calm talk gives her a chance to apologise and fix it.
Why do grandparents often repeat the same stories?
They enjoy them and want them remembered. Because the stories hold their happiest memories, and repeating them is a way to share love and pass on family history.
What is a good way to welcome a new student who joins mid-year?
Greet her, ask her name and invite her to sit with you. Because a new student knows nobody, and a simple friendly step helps her feel she belongs.
Why does it hurt when a friend breaks a promise?
Because we trusted what the friend said. We had planned around it, so the broken promise feels like we did not matter, even if there was a good reason.
Why do people hold the door for the person behind them?
It is a small act of care. Because it costs little effort and saves the other person from a door swinging into them, and it makes both feel considerate.
Why might a shy child need more time before joining a game?
A shy child likes to watch and feel safe first. Because new groups feel risky to such a child, and watching helps the child learn the rules and see that others are friendly.
Why is it better to ask than to take someone's pen without telling them?
Asking respects the owner. Because the person may need the pen at that moment, and taking it quietly can look like stealing even if you meant to return it.
A teacher praised only one student. Why might others feel left out?
They wanted the same recognition. Because people like to feel noticed for their effort, and when only one gets praise the rest may think their work counted for less.
Why do we say excuse me when we pass in front of someone?
It shows we know we are disturbing them. Because stepping through their space without a word feels rude, and the phrase tells them we mean no disrespect.
Why do some people laugh when they are nervous?
The laugh releases tension. Because the body is full of worry and laughter is one way to let some of that energy out, even though nothing is funny.
My younger brother copies everything I do. Why does he do that?
He looks up to you. Because young children learn by watching those they admire, and an older sibling is the person closest to them to learn from.
Should you tell a teacher if a classmate is being bullied?
Yes, you should tell a trusted adult. Because the person being bullied may be too scared to speak up, and a teacher can stop it in ways a classmate cannot.
Why does it feel good to finish a hard task?
Finishing gives a sense of pride. Because the effort paid off, and the mind rewards us with a good feeling that makes us want to try difficult things again.
Why do neighbours greet each other even if they do not know one another well?
A greeting builds goodwill. Because people who live close share space, and a smile or hello makes the area feel safe and friendly.
Why might a person say they are fine when they are not?
They may not want to worry others or may not feel ready to talk. Because saying more feels hard, so a short answer protects them until they are comfortable.
A friend always arrives late. What is a kind way to deal with it?
Explain how it affects you and ask what is making her late. Because a calm talk can solve the real problem, while scolding mainly makes people feel attacked.
Why do people stand when the national anthem plays?
Standing shows respect. Because the anthem stands for the country and its people, and a shared posture shows that everyone honours it together.
Why do guests often bring a small gift when they visit?
It is a way of saying thanks for the welcome. Because the host spends time and effort on the guest, and a gift shows appreciation in return.
Why does a team need a captain?
Someone has to make quick decisions and keep everyone together. Because a group with no leader may argue over what to do, and a captain helps turn many ideas into one plan.
Why should you say what you feel instead of slamming a door?
Words explain what is wrong. Because a slammed door only tells people that you are upset, so they may guess wrongly, while a clear sentence helps them understand and help.
What does it show when a person remembers your birthday without being told?
It shows they care about you. Because remembering takes attention and effort, and people usually spend that on someone who matters to them.
Why do children get excited the night before a festival?
They are looking forward to something enjoyable. Because the mind keeps picturing the sweets, new clothes and family visits, and that eager feeling makes it hard to settle down.
Is it fine to make fun of someone's accent?
No, it is not. Because the accent is part of where the person comes from, and mocking it can make them feel they do not belong.
A friend won the race and I came last. How can I still be a good friend?
Congratulate her warmly. Because her win is not taken from you, and being glad for her keeps the friendship strong while you can still feel proud of trying.
Why do shopkeepers say thank you after a sale?
It shows they value the customer. Because a customer could have gone elsewhere, and a friendly word makes people want to come back.
Why do some students prefer to study in groups?
Talking about the lesson helps them remember it. Because friends can explain the parts others missed, and the group keeps each person motivated.
If I hear a rumour about a friend, should I pass it on?
No, it is better not to. Because a rumour may not be true, and spreading it can hurt your friend and make others think less of you.
Why do people feel calmer after taking a few slow breaths?
Slow breathing tells the body it is safe. Because it slows the heartbeat, and a slower heartbeat makes the mind feel less alarmed.
On a crowded bus, why do we offer our seat to an older person?
Standing is harder for them. Because older people tire quickly and may lose balance when the bus jerks, and giving a seat is a simple way to show care.
Why do siblings often fight over small things?
They live close together and compete for attention. Because they share space and parents, small things like a toy or a seat can feel unfair, and they do not hold back their feelings at home.
Why do some people go quiet when they are angry?
They are trying to avoid saying something they will regret. Because silence gives time to cool down, and some people feel safer thinking before they speak.
If your clothes catch fire, what is the first thing to do?
Stop, drop and roll on the ground. Because running feeds the flames with more air, while rolling smothers the fire and keeps it from reaching your face.
Is it safe to cross the road while looking at your phone?
No, it is not safe. Because your eyes and attention are on the screen, so you may miss a vehicle that is coming and not hear the horn.
If you smell gas in the kitchen, should you switch on the light to check?
No, do not touch any switch. Because a tiny spark from the switch can set the gas on fire. Open the windows, turn off the cylinder and get out to tell an adult.
Why should you never mix different cleaning liquids at home?
They can react and give off harmful fumes. Because chemicals made for different jobs may combine into new substances that are poisonous to breathe.
If you get lost at a crowded fair, what is the best move?
Stay where you are and ask a shopkeeper or a police officer for help. Because your family will go back to look for you at the place they last saw you, and moving around makes you harder to find.
Why do we wear a helmet when riding a bicycle?
It protects the head in a fall. Because the skull is hard but the brain inside is soft, and a helmet spreads out the force of a knock so less of it reaches the head.
Should you pour water on a pan of burning oil?
No, never. Because water sinks under the oil and turns to steam in an instant, which throws burning oil out of the pan and spreads the fire. Cover the pan with a lid instead.
Why must we wash our hands before eating?
Hands pick up germs from everything we touch. Because germs on the fingers can pass into the mouth with food, and soap with water washes them off.
Why is it unwise to run near a swimming pool?
The edge is wet and slippery. Because wet tiles give shoes little grip, so you may slip and hit the ground or fall in.
Why should a stranger not be told where you live?
The stranger may not mean well. Because you cannot know a person's real purpose from a short meeting, and an address could be used to find you.
What is the safest way to carry scissors to another person?
Hold them by the closed blades with the handle pointing towards the person. Because the sharp tip is then pointing away from both of you, so nobody gets cut if you slip.
Why do we keep medicines out of young children's reach?
Children may mistake them for sweets. Because even a medicine that helps an adult can harm a small body, and young children cannot judge what is safe to swallow.
Is it a good idea to shelter under a tree in a thunderstorm?
No, it is not. Because lightning often strikes the tallest thing around, and a tall wet tree can pass the strike on to anyone standing close.
What makes the footpath a better place to walk than the road?
The footpath keeps you away from moving vehicles. Because drivers cannot always stop in time, and a strip set apart from traffic lowers the chance of being hit.
Before climbing a ladder, what should I check?
Check that it stands firm on level ground. Because a ladder on a slope or loose ground can slip when you climb, and a fall from a height can badly hurt you.
Why do we let hot food cool a little before giving it to a baby?
A baby's mouth is very sensitive. Because food that feels warm to an adult can burn a baby's soft skin and tongue.
Why is it risky to leave a pot handle sticking out over the edge of the stove?
Someone could knock it. Because a child or a passer-by may bump the handle, and the hot contents would spill and burn them.
Why should you keep a charger away from water?
Water can carry electricity where it should not go. Because a wet plug or wire may give a shock or cause a short circuit and a fire.
What is the right thing to do if you find a sharp object, like a broken glass, on the playground?
Tell a teacher instead of picking it up. Because bare hands can be cut badly, and an adult has the right tools to remove it safely.
Why do we use a seat belt even on a short trip?
Accidents can happen at any distance. Because in a sudden stop your body keeps moving forward at the speed of the car, and the belt holds you in your seat.
Why do we keep the cupboard door shut after taking something out?
An open door can hit someone. Because people walking in the room may not see it and bump their head, and a closed door also keeps the shelves tidy.
Why is it important to look both ways even on a one-way street?
A vehicle may still come from the unexpected side. Because cyclists or careless drivers sometimes go the wrong way, so a quick look on both sides costs little and may save you.
Can I pet a stray dog while it is eating?
Better not to. Because a dog guarding its food may bite out of instinct, and it does not know you mean no harm.
Why do we tie our hair back near a flame or a machine?
Loose hair can catch fire or get pulled in. Because strands near a flame can ignite easily, and a machine with moving parts can grab hair and drag the head with it.
Why do swimmers wait before going into the water after a heavy meal?
The body is busy digesting. Because a full stomach can make swimming uncomfortable, so most people prefer to rest a little first.
Why does a mother tell her child to chew food well?
Chewing breaks food into small pieces. Because small pieces are easier to swallow and to digest, and they are less likely to get stuck in the throat.
What is the reason a teacher asks the class to line up quietly during a fire drill?
Calm lines get everyone out faster. Because pushing and shouting cause falls and block the way, and the teacher can then hear the instructions and count the students.
Why is it unwise to stay up very late before an exam?
You will be tired in the exam. Because sleep helps the brain sort and store what you learned, and a tired mind finds it hard to focus and remember.
Why do we stay in the shade during the hottest part of the day?
Too much heat can make us ill. Because the sun at midday is strongest, and shade keeps the body from overheating and losing too much water.
What happens if you do not drink enough water on a hot day?
You may feel tired and get a headache. Because the body loses water through sweat, and without enough of it the body cannot work well.
Why should you wipe up a spill on the floor right away?
Someone may slip on it. Because a wet floor is slippery and people do not expect it, so a fall can happen in an instant.
Why do we switch off the iron when we leave the room?
A hot iron can start a fire. Because it stays hot for a long time, and if it touches cloth or paper the heat can set them alight.
Why do we cover a sneeze with an elbow or tissue?
It keeps the germs from spreading. Because a sneeze sends tiny drops a long way, and covering it catches them before they reach others.
Why does a teacher keep chemicals in a locked cupboard?
Some of them can burn or poison. Because students may not know what each one can do, so keeping them locked stops accidents.
Why should you take off muddy shoes at the door?
The mud stays outside. Because shoes carry dirt and germs from the street, and leaving them at the door keeps the floors clean for people who sit on them or walk barefoot.
Why do you keep the fridge door closed as much as possible?
The cold stays inside. Because an open door lets warm air in, and the fridge then has to work harder and the food may spoil sooner.
Why do we throw rubbish in a bin instead of on the street?
The street would get dirty and unsafe. Because rubbish attracts flies and rats, blocks drains and can hurt animals that eat it.
Why do doctors and nurses wear masks during surgery?
The mask keeps germs from the mouth and nose off the patient. Because an open wound can get infected easily, and every breath puts tiny drops into the air.
Why do cyclists need a light at night?
Others can see them. Because a dark road hides a bike, and a light lets drivers spot the cyclist from far away in time to slow down.
In a fire, why are stairs better than a lift?
A lift can stop working. Because the power may fail and trap people inside, while stairs always let them walk out.
Why should a parent hold a young child's hand on a busy road?
The child cannot judge traffic yet. Because small children can dart out suddenly, and a held hand stops them before they step into danger.
Why do we leave a gap between our vehicle and the one ahead?
It gives time to stop. Because a vehicle cannot halt at once, and if the one ahead brakes suddenly, a gap lets us stop without hitting it.
Why do trains have a loud horn?
The horn warns people. Because a heavy train needs a long distance to stop, so people on the track must hear it early and get out of the way.
A friend has a small cut at school. What do I do?
Take her to the teacher or the nurse. Because the cut needs to be cleaned and covered by someone who knows how, so it does not get infected.
Why do we avoid eating food that has been left open for a long time?
It may have germs. Because flies and dust can land on it, and germs grow quickly in food that is not covered or kept cool, which can make us sick.
Why does a teacher ask students to keep their bags out of the aisle?
People can trip over them. Because bags on the floor are hard to see in a crowded room, and a fall in a classroom can hurt someone and block the way out.
Is it safe to run with a pencil in your hand?
No, it is not safe. Because if you fall, the sharp point can poke your skin or eye as you land on it. It is safer to carry it with the tip pointing down.
Why do we wait for the green light even when the road looks empty?
A vehicle could appear suddenly. Because drivers do not expect a person to cross against the signal, and the rule keeps everyone predictable and safe.
Which should you do first when you get ready for school: pack your bag or put on your shoes?
Pack your bag first, then put on your shoes. Because shoes at the door mean you are leaving, and you do not want to walk around the house in them or find at the last minute that you forgot something.
If it starts to rain while you are at the park, what is the sensible thing to do?
Find a shelter and wait there. Because getting soaked can make you cold, and a covered spot keeps you dry until the rain eases or someone comes to fetch you.
I want to bake a cake but I have no eggs. What can I do?
Check whether a recipe without eggs is possible, or ask a neighbour for some. Because eggs hold a cake together, so leaving them out without changing anything may give a flat, crumbly result.
A recipe says to boil the water before adding the rice. Why does the order matter?
The rice cooks evenly in boiling water. Because if it is added to cold water, it sits and turns mushy while the water slowly warms.
All birds have feathers. A penguin is a bird. Does a penguin have feathers?
Yes, it does. Because the rule says every bird has feathers, so anything that is a bird must have them too.
All the children in the class like cricket. Meena likes cricket. Is she certainly in that class?
No, we cannot be sure. Because the rule only says the children in the class like cricket, and other people outside the class may also like it.
If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. What can we say about the rain?
It did not rain, at least not enough to matter. Because if it had rained, the rule says the match would have been cancelled, and it was not.
Ravi is taller than Sunil, and Sunil is taller than Tara. Who is the shortest?
Tara is the shortest. Because Ravi is taller than Sunil, Sunil is taller than Tara, so Tara is below both of them in height.
The bell rings after the last lesson. The bell has just rung. What has just ended?
The last lesson has just ended. Because the bell is the signal that comes after the last lesson, so hearing it tells us that lesson is over.
Which comes first, the seed or the fruit?
The seed comes first in a new plant's life. Because the plant grows from the seed, flowers, and only then makes fruit that holds new seeds, so the seed starts the cycle again.
If you want to send a letter, what has to happen before the postman can deliver it?
You must write the address on it and post it. Because the postman reads the address to know where it goes, and a letter that is never posted cannot be collected.
My friend says she always wins at carrom, but she lost today. Was she lying?
Not necessarily. Because people often say always when they mean usually, and one loss does not prove that her words were meant to deceive.
If the plant dies after we stop watering it, does that prove the lack of water killed it?
It is a strong clue but not proof. Because other things like too little light or poor soil could also harm it, so we would need to check them before we know for sure.
Why does it help to make a list before going to the market?
A list reminds you what you need. Because it is easy to forget things in a busy market, and a list also helps you avoid buying things you do not need.
What is the harm in answering a question before reading it fully?
You may miss part of what is asked. Because the last words often change the meaning, so a quick guess can give a good answer to the wrong question.
I cannot find my school bag this morning. Where do I look?
Think about where you last used it and look there first. Because bags usually stay near the place you finished with them, and a calm search saves more time than hunting everywhere.
If every road in the town leads to the market, and I am on a road, can I reach the market?
Yes, you can. Because the rule says that every road leads there, so following the road you are on will take you to the market.
Does a wet road always mean it rained?
No, it does not. Because a water tanker, a burst pipe or someone washing a car could also leave the road wet, so rain is only one possible cause.
Why do we make a plan before starting a big project at school?
A plan breaks the job into steps. Because a large task feels less scary in small parts, and the plan tells us what to do first and what we may need to ask for.
I have a test tomorrow and a game tonight. How can I decide what to do?
Think about which matters more and whether both are possible. Because you may be able to study first and play later, and weighing the two helps you avoid regrets.
Why should you set out your uniform the night before school?
It saves time in the morning. Because you can spot a missing button or a dirty shirt while there is still time to fix it, and the morning goes more smoothly.
If the shop is closed on Sundays and today is Sunday, can I buy bread there?
No, you cannot. Because the shop does not open on Sundays, so you will need to go to another shop or wait for Monday.
A rope bridge is old and its planks look cracked. Should we cross it one by one or all together?
One by one is wiser, and better still is to find another way. Because the load on the bridge is lighter when only one person is on it, and cracked planks may not hold the whole group.
When packing a shopping bag, why go with the heavy things at the bottom?
Heavy things crush light things on top. Because eggs, bread or fruit under a tin would be squashed, and the bag is also easier to carry when its weight is low.
If I water the plant today, do I need to water it again tomorrow?
Not always. Because wet soil keeps water for some time, so you should touch the soil first and water again only when it feels dry.
After playing, why should toys be put away?
Toys left around can get lost or broken. Because someone may step on them and slip, and putting them back lets you find them easily the next time.
If the bus is crowded, should I wait for the next one when I am in a hurry?
It depends on how long the next one takes. Because a crowded bus is uncomfortable but may get you there sooner, while waiting could make you later than a crowded ride would.
When you make tea with milk and water together, which can you add last: the sugar or the tea leaves?
Add the sugar last. Because sugar dissolves easily in hot tea at any point, while the leaves need time in the hot water to give their flavour, so they must go in earlier.
Why is it good to read the instructions before putting together a new cupboard?
The steps usually go in a fixed order. Because a wrong early step can mean taking everything apart to fix it, and reading first shows which parts go where.
The teacher said the one who finishes first can leave. Does that mean the one who finishes last can never leave?
No, that would be going too far. Because the teacher only said that the first to finish may leave early, and everyone can leave once the work is done.
If you want to catch a train that leaves early in the morning, what should you do the night before?
Pack your things and set an alarm. Because rushing in the morning leads to forgotten items, and a good alarm helps you wake up with enough time.
A shirt shrank in the wash. What might have gone wrong?
It was probably washed in water that was too hot. Because heat makes some cloth fibres tighten up, so the shirt came out smaller than before.
Before a long walk, why fill a water bottle?
There may be no place to drink on the way. Because walking makes us thirsty, and having water with us means we do not have to go without.
If two paths lead to the same village and one is blocked by a fallen tree, which should you take?
Take the clear path. Because both go to the same place, so the open path gets you there without delay or the risk of climbing over a tree.
My little sister cries when she is hungry. How can I tell the difference from other kinds of crying?
Look at the time and what else is happening. Because hunger crying often comes near mealtime and stops when she eats, while crying from tiredness or pain has other signs.
Why do we label jars in the kitchen?
The jars look alike. Because sugar, salt and flour all look white, and a label lets anyone pick the right one without tasting or guessing.
If a pen stops writing, what simple things can we try before throwing it away?
Try it on rough paper and shake it, or check whether the cap sealed it. Because the ink may be dry at the tip or stuck, and a little scribbling can bring it back.
Why should you start homework with the hardest subject?
Your mind is fresh at the start. Because hard tasks need the most thought, and doing them first leaves the easy ones for when you are tired.
If you hear someone knocking at the door, what should a child do when alone at home?
Ask who it is through the door and not open for a stranger. Because you cannot see a person's intention, and a locked door keeps you safe until a trusted grown-up decides.
Can a person be at the library and at the playground at the same moment?
No, one person cannot be in two places at once. Because a body takes up one spot, so he must leave the library before he can arrive at the playground.
Which is the better way to learn a poem: read it once aloud or read it many times?
Read it many times. Because repeating helps the words stay in memory, while a single reading fades quickly.
What is the use of writing a name on a school water bottle?
Many bottles look alike. Because a name lets us tell ours from the others and helps a lost bottle find its way back to us.
A candle burns down faster on a windy night. Why?
The wind feeds the flame with fresh air. Because a flame burns hotter with more air, and the wind also makes the wax melt and run off quicker.
If I plant a mango seed today, can I eat mangoes from it next week?
No, you cannot. Because a mango seed takes a very long time to grow into a tree that bears fruit, and it needs years of care before that happens.
Why do we put a bookmark in a book?
It shows where we stopped. Because we can then return to the exact page, and we do not have to flip through it or risk bending the corner.
When a lamp stops working, what is the first thing to check?
Check whether it is plugged in and switched on. Because the simplest causes are the most common, and the bulb or wiring need not be touched if the power is just off.
Why does a teacher give a warning before a test?
Students need time to prepare. Because a test checks what we know, and with notice we can revise, which makes the result fairer and the day less stressful.
If someone gives you wrong directions, how can you still find your way?
Ask another person and compare. Because one answer may be a mistake, and two people agreeing makes it more likely to be right.
Why do travellers carry a torch on a dark road?
It lights the path. Because they can then see holes, stones and animals ahead, and others can see them too.
Why should you read a story twice if you did not understand it at first?
The second reading often shows what you missed. Because you now know how it ends, so the earlier clues make sense and the details fall into place.
When a kettle is left to boil for ages with nobody watching, what can go wrong?
The water can boil away and the kettle can get damaged. Because the heat keeps coming even after the water is gone, so the empty kettle overheats and may start to burn.
Sana's umbrella is wet after the walk home. Should she close it and leave it standing or open it to dry?
Opening it to dry is better. Because the water on the cloth can spread out and evaporate faster, and a closed damp umbrella can stay wet and grow mould.
